proposals.prompt:
Agents in a supermarket gridworld must collect their required items and leave through the exit. Every action costs the same, so demonstrators prefer short trajectories -- unless an unknown social norm makes them behave otherwise. Your task is to propose candidate norms (obligations or prohibitions) that could explain the demonstrated behaviour.
Each demonstration is listed step by step as  `k: {atoms true in the state} action`.

Available atoms:
- at(x,y) -- the agent is at cell (x,y); x = column (0 = left), y = row (0 = top); N decreases y, S increases y, E increases x, W decreases x
- actions N, S, E, W, MOVE (any of the four moves), INTERACT (any interaction with an object: the different kinds of interaction are NOT distinguished), EXIT (leave the store; always the last action)

Demonstration 1 (required items: apple, eggs):

  1: {at(1,5)} INTERACT

 34: {at(9,5)} <terminal>

Propose norms using ONLY the atoms listed above. Do NOT define any new state properties or events: "abstraction" must be {}.
Propose 8 diverse candidate hypotheses.

Output format: return ONLY a JSON list (no prose, no code fences). Each element:
{"id": short_name, "text": one-sentence natural-language statement of the norm,
 "abstraction": {"state_properties": {name: FORMULA, ...},
                 "events": {name: {"pre": FORMULA, "post": FORMULA or null}, ...}},
 "norm": {"type": "prohibition", "condition": FORMULA}
       | {"type": "obligation", "trigger": FORMULA or "START", "discharge": FORMULA}}
FORMULA := atom | name of a property/event defined in this hypothesis | {"not": F} | {"and": [F, ...]}
         | {"or": [F, ...]} | {"le"|"lt"|"ge"|"gt"|"eq": [numeric_feature, integer]}
Semantics.  A trajectory is a sequence of steps (state s_k, action a_k).  A step's label contains the atoms true in
s_k and the action a_k.  A state property is a formula over state atoms (no actions).  An event
{"pre": P, "post": Q} occurs at step k when P holds for the label of step k and Q holds in the next state s_{k+1}
(post may be null).  A prohibition counts one violation for every step whose label (including events occurring at
that step) satisfies the condition.  An obligation becomes pending at any step satisfying the trigger ("START" =
pending from the beginning) and is fulfilled by a later (or the same) step satisfying the discharge; it can be
triggered again; it is violated if it is still pending when the trajectory ends.

parsed.text: A shopper should check out the entrance cart before doing the trip through the store.
Items should be picked up only while the shopper has the cart, not while walking without it.
A shopper should not carry merchandise by hand when the cart system is available.
After taking a cart, the shopper is obliged to return it to the cart-return bay before the trip ends.
A shopper may put the cart down only at the designated cart-return bay.
A shopper should not leave the supermarket while still possessing the cart.
Once the cart has been returned, the shopper should not do any further store interactions and should simply proceed to the exit.
Carts are prohibited in the pedestrian checkout and exit zone on the east side of the store.

parsed.text: A shopper should check out the entrance cart before doing the trip through the store.
Items should be picked up only while the shopper has the cart, not while walking without it.
A shopper should not carry merchandise by hand when the cart system is available.
After taking a cart, the shopper is obliged to return it to the cart-return bay before the trip ends.
A shopper may put the cart down only at the designated cart-return bay.
A shopper should not leave the supermarket while still possessing the cart.
Once the cart has been returned, the shopper should not do any further store interactions and should simply proceed to the exit.
Carts are prohibited in the pedestrian checkout and exit zone on the east side of the store.

[g1_items_only_with_cart] FORBIDDEN: item_pickup_without_cart  where shopper_has_cart := hasCart; shopper_without_cart := ¬hasCart; item_pickup_without_cart := (PICKUP_ITEM ∧ shopper_without_cart)
[g1_no_hand_carrying] FORBIDDEN: carrying_item_by_hand  where carrying_item_by_hand := handFull; become_hand_loaded := ¬handFull · handFull

[g1_return_cart_to_bay] OBLIGED: after cart_taken, eventually return_cart_to_bay (before exit)  where cart_parked_in_return_bay := cartAt(0,1); cart_return_bay := at(0,1); cart_taken := PICKUP_CART · hasCart; return_cart_to_bay := (cart_return_bay ∧ LEAVE_CART) · cart_parked_in_return_bay

[g1_leave_cart_only_at_bay] FORBIDDEN: leave_cart_outside_bay  where cart_return_bay := at(0,1); outside_cart_return_bay := ¬cart_return_bay; leave_cart_outside_bay := (LEAVE_CART ∧ outside_cart_return_bay)
[g1_no_exit_with_cart] FORBIDDEN: exit_while_pushing_cart  where shopper_has_cart := hasCart; exit_while_pushing_cart := (EXIT ∧ shopper_has_cart)
[g1_cart_return_final_interaction] FORBIDDEN: post_return_interaction  where cart_parked_in_return_bay := cartAt(0,1); post_return_interaction := (cart_parked_in_return_bay ∧ INTERACT)

[g1_cart_free_exit_zone] FORBIDDEN: cart_in_pedestrian_exit_zone  where cart_in_pedestrian_exit_zone := (hasCart ∧ pedestrian_exit_zone); pedestrian_exit_zone := (at(7,2) ∨ at(8,2) ∨ at(9,2) ∨ at(7,3) ∨ at(8,3) ∨ at(9,3) ∨ at(7,4) ∨ at(8,4) ∨ at(9,4) ∨ at(7,5) ∨ at(8,5) ∨ at(9,5)); move_cart_into_exit_zone := (hasCart ∧ MOVE) · pedestrian_exit_zone
